description: Readings that differ on purpose from the reference dictionary used by tools/check-pronunciation.mjs (to-jyutping). Each needs a reason.

notes.reason: Hong Kong usage for 'upload' reads 上 as soeng5 (the verb 'go up'), as in 上網 soeng5 mong5.
The question particle 嗎 is maa3 in standard Jyutping (LSHK); maa1 is a less common variant. Kept consistent with the pattern maa3-question.
The question particle 嗎 is maa3 in standard Jyutping (LSHK); maa1 is a less common variant.
出面 'outside' is ceot1 min6 in everyday speech; min2 is a changed-tone variant.
Both bin1 and bin6 are heard for 'side'; bin1 matches the written 邊 (bin6 is usually written 便).
Both bin1 and bin6 are heard for 'side'; bin1 matches the written 邊 (bin6 is usually written 便).
Verb + 吓 'briefly, a little' (睇吓, 試吓) is haa5; haa2 is a different interjection.
呢 'this' is read ni1 or nei1; ni1 is the more common pronunciation among younger Hong Kong speakers and the one taught here throughout.
In the set phrase 唔好意思 'sorry, excuse me', 思 is said si3; si1 is the reading in 意思 'meaning'.
The exclamation 'wow' is usually waa3 when expressing surprise at something seen; waa1 is also heard.
Colloquial reading: 坐 'sit; travel by' is co5 in everyday speech; zo6 is the literary reading.
女 'daughter' (個女) takes the changed tone neoi2; neoi5 means 'female' in compounds such as 女人.
姨姨 'auntie' (mother's sister) is commonly ji4 ji1; ji1 ji1 is also heard.
寫字樓 'office building' keeps 樓 as lau4.
Reduplicated 慢慢 takes a changed tone on the second syllable (maan6 maan2), and 行 'walk' is haang4; hang4 means 'row' or 'bank'.
房 'room' (間房) is said with the changed tone fong2 when it stands alone.
樓 meaning 'flat, property' (買樓, 啲樓) takes the changed tone lau2; lau4 is 'floor, building'.
As the classifier for a plate of food (一碟腸粉), 碟 is said dip2.
翳 is standardly ai3 with no initial; ngai3 is a common variant.
The resultative complement 到 is very often said with the changed tone dou2 (聽到, 見到); the pattern dou2-result teaches this form.
袋 'bag' (膠袋, 個袋) is said doi2 when it stands alone.
The polite set phrase 請問 'excuse me, may I ask' uses the literary reading cing2; ceng2 is used for 'invite, treat'.
故事 'story' is gu3 si6; gu2 belongs to the different expression 講古 'tell old stories'.
Turning (轉左, 轉右, 轉彎) is zyun3; zyun2 is 'to transfer, pass on'.
Turning (轉左, 轉右, 轉彎) is zyun3; zyun2 is 'to transfer, pass on'.
Colloquial reading: 近 'near' is kan5 in speech; gan6 is literary (附近 fu6 gan6).
返 'return; back' is faan1 both as a verb (返屋企) and after a verb (攞返); faan2 is a rarer variant.
返 'go (back) to' is faan1, as in 返工 faan1 gung1.
魚 'fish' as food or on its own (食魚) is commonly said with the changed tone jyu2.
黑 is standardly hak1; haak1 is a colloquial variant. 黑雨 is the black rainstorm warning.
The friendly particle 呀 is aa3 in replies such as 唔係呀; aa5 is a less common variant.
Answering the phone, 喂 is said with a rising tone, wai2; wai3 is the call 'hey!'.
卡 'card' (from English 'card'), as in 碌卡 and 八達通卡, is kaat1; kaa1 is 'to get stuck'.
左右 'about, approximately' after a number is zo2 jau6; jau2 is a casual changed tone.
會 'a meeting' is wui2 (changed tone), as in 開會 hoi1 wui2; when 緊 splits the verb (開緊會) it stands alone. wui5 is the modal 'will'.
